pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages - Spanish
Learning a foreign language is a liberation from insularity and provides an opening to other cultures. A high-quality languages education should foster pupils’ curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world. The teaching should enable pupils to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing. It should also provide opportunities for them to communicate for practical purposes, learn new ways of thinking and read great literature in the original language. Language teaching should provide the foundation for learning further languages, equipping pupils to study and work in other countries.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Making everyday a successful learning journey
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will undertake. Hawkedale is a delightful Primary school that our children, staff and governors are proud of. We provide a caring and supportive environment, and we have high expectations of success.
Every child can make good progress, not just in their academic life, but in their personal and social development as well. We expect our children to grow up to be accepting of others, make good moral choices and be active members of the community.
We provide our pupils with an innovative curriculum, and constantly review and evaluate the achievements of the school. We provide high academic standards, as well as ensuring all children make the levels of progress that they are capable of.
We believe that we can only achieve the best for your child through a close co-operation between home and school and we aim to involve parents as much as possible.
We enjoy showing parents around our school, so that the family atmosphere and ethos can be experienced first hand. We embrace this as an opportunity to explain our aims and to answer any questions you may have.
Mrs J Davies, Headteacher
Hawkedale pupils stand out. Their conduct and manners are impeccable. They are cheery and cordial in their exchanges with everyone. Parents are delighted with how the school nurtures their children. Staff care deeply about the pupils and the school feels like a family.'' (Ofsted 2022)

SEND
Our Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCO) is Mrs L Pugh.
Email: senco@hawkedale.surrey.sch.uk
At Hawkedale Primary School we believe a child-centred approach is an integral part in the quality of teaching and learning across the whole curriculum. We are fully committed to offering an inclusive and balanced curriculum that all pupils can participate in.
We believe that all children have an equal right to a full and rounded education which will enable them to achieve their full potential – academically, socially, physically and emotionally.
All our teachers see themselves as teachers of SEND and consistently follow the ‘assess, plan, do and review’ approach to making sure they can address and respond to the diversity of needs of each individual child.
Please read our full SEND policy to find out more about how we identify, provide for, assess and challenge our children with SEND.
The school is fully compliant with the DDA (Disability Discrimination Act), please see Accessibility Plan listed below.

The Curriculum
During your child’s time at Hawkedale Primary School they will experience a broad, creative and exciting curriculum, which we hope will help develop in them a love of lifelong learning and the skills, knowledge and values to help them as they continue to the next phase of their education and out into the wider world.
We believe children learn better, when they are encouraged to use their imagination and apply their learning to engaging contexts. We use memorable experiences such as educational trips, workshops and fun activities to enhance the learning.

Clubs
Hawkedale Primary offers a variety of after school clubs termly. Club places will be offered on a first-come-first-serve basis. Clubs are run termly and your child will need to re-apply to clubs at the start of each term.
The clubs run from 3.10 -4.10pm,
Please may I remind you that if your child in not going to attend a club on a particular day then it is imperative you notify the club teacher of your child’s absence. It is your responsibility to collect your child from school as soon as the clubs finish each day. Please note that owing to after school meetings and/or courses clubs may have to be cancelled on occasions, we will endeavour to give as much notice as we can of cancellations.

pageCache.text:
Early Years
Welcome to Puffin Class!
We at Hawkedale recognise how important and special the first year of school is to our children. Our aim in reception is for all of our children to become happy independent learners and we achieve this by building the following skills…
to build relationships through being kind, respectful and co-operative,
to feel safe in their learning environment and with the people around them,
to know there is always someone to help you,
and to smile everyday!
Independence is… to be confident to try new things,
to be a good listener and communicator,
to show resilience because some things take practise
and to have self-belief that YOU CAN DO IT!
to be challenged with new knowledge and skills,
to accept it is ok to make mistakes because that is how we will learn
and to gain a love for experiencing new learning adventures.
We start the year by ensuring the children are comfortable with their new environment, within the classroom and the wider school so they can move around confidently. We focus on building friendships and positive relationships with peers and staff members through communication so that we can enjoy a year together full of fun exploration and learning.
At Hawkedale, we recognise the importance of providing a variety of learning experiences for the children. They will learn through teacher led activities, which may be whole class, small group or individual learning. There will be teacher-initiated activities, which are planned and provided by the adult but the children carry out independently. Finally there is child led experiences that children control in terms of resources, time and outcome. The children have access to the inside and outside classroom all day and in all weathers too.
Children in Reception Class follow the Foundation Stage Curriculum as set out by Government guidelines.
The curriculum is divided into seven key areas which cover all aspects of the child’s development: Personal Social Emotional development, Communication and Language, Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding of the World and Expressive Arts and Design

pageCache.pageTitle: Start and End of Day arrangements - Hawkedale Primary School
pageCache.text:
Start and End of Day arrangements
The school gates open at 8.30am and a member of staff will be at each gate ready to greet the children and take any messages you may have for the staff.
School begins with registration at 8.40 am, this 10 minutes gives the children time to say their goodbyes, change their reading books, hang up their coats and put away their fruit.
Children need to be in class and ready for learning by 8.40am.
It is important that you are punctual as children miss valuable learning time if they are regularly late. It can also trigger a visit from the Education Inclusion Officer. If children arrive after the close of register at 9.00am then they are marked as being absent for the morning session.
If you are going to be late for whatever reason, please call the office and let us know as we can then book your child a school lunch and mark the register accordingly.
If your child is going to be absent from school due to illness please could you let the office know before 9.15am.
A leave of absence is only granted for exceptional circumstances and if an application is made in advance. An application form can be obtained from the school office.
Doctor and dentist appointments during the school day should be avoided.
A copy of the appointment letter or card is required to authorise the leave of absence.
School finishes at 3.10 pm for EYFS and KS1 children and 3.10pm for KS2 children. The children are to be collected from the playground from their class teachers.
